newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former Japan bureaucrat arrested for bribery.
newsitem.headline: Former Japan bureaucrat arrested for bribery.

text.p: A scandal involving Japanese bureaucrats and an oil trader under arrest for fraud widened on Thursday when a former senior transport official was arrested for receiving bribes.

A police spokesman said Tsuneharu Hattori, former president of Osaka's Kansai International Airport Co. was arrested for receiving bribes from Junichi Izui, an oil trader arrested for fraud and tax evasion charges.
Police said Izui paid the bribe to ensure a cleaning company was awarded a contract at the country's second-largest airport.

Izui, owner of an Osaka-based oil firm, was arrested in November on suspicion of evading income tax on oil deal commissions. He was arrested again in early January on fraud charges along with two former oil company executives.
The oil trader has boasted of close ties to high-ranking politicians and bureaucrats.
Hattori was vice transport minister before taking up the post of president at the Kansai airport.
The police spokesman said Hattori was suspected of receiving gold ingots and artwork from Izui worth about 1.4 million yen ($11,700).
Last month, Japan's trade ministry punished several senior bureaucrats for receiving excessive entertainment from Izui although the ministry denied any illegal acts in the contacts.
